title: Consent, Secrets, and a Decision That Is Theirs

questions.stem: The form is signed. Is that enough to say the patient consented?

options.text: Yes; the form is the consent
No; the form is only the record. You still need understanding and a voluntary choice

questions.explanation: Ask the patient to say it back.

questions.stem: A capable patient refuses a transfusion the team thinks is clearly better. What stands?

options.text: Ending the relationship on the spot

questions.explanation: Disagreement is not incapacity. You do not abandon them.

options.text: No chest compressions and no restart of the heart; it is not a stop to comfort or ordinary care

questions.explanation: Ask what else they still want.

options.text: To anyone in the hallway who asks
For a serious, imminent threat, and only as much as that threat requires

questions.explanation: Tell the patient what you must disclose, unless telling them would itself cause the harm.

questions.stem: If no one can consent in time in a true emergency:

options.text: You must wait, even if delay would cause harm
Emergency care that a reasonable person would want may proceed
You may also do an unrelated elective procedure

questions.explanation: This is not a blank check for elective care.

questions.stem: Withdrawing a ventilator, compared with never starting it, is ethically:

options.text: A reason to ignore a capable refusal of blood

questions.explanation: Withholding and withdrawing are ethically equivalent.

questions.stem: You disagree with a patient and want to end the relationship. You must:

options.text: Walk out of an emergency and leave no plan
Give notice and a way to continue care
Refuse all further conversation the same day, with no handoff
Move a friend up a list instead

questions.explanation: A disagreement is not abandonment, but ending care still requires a safe handoff.

options.text: A fair clinical rule stated in advance

questions.explanation: Justice is the fair share, not the loudest request.

options.text: Be the interpreter for a consent conversation
Not be the interpreter; use a professional interpreter
Sign the form instead of the patient
You do not abandon a patient you disagree with.

questions.explanation: A do-not-resuscitate order is not a do-not-treat order.
